correctness.rationale: Greedy subsequence matching in the ordered cyclic period incurs precisely one period per weak descent. In a square UU the cost is 1+2r+s. Matrix trace of M_q(z^2)^(m-1) M_q(z) marks all roots once. Writing M_q(t)=(1-t)U+tJ, nilpotence of U, determinant lemma and Jacobi derivative yield the rational formula; proof is formal and valid for every q>=2. Symbol frequency bounds m<=q floor(k/2). Equality forces h full strict circular runs and cyclic rotations, with endpoint s selecting one rotation for even k and all q for odd k. The actual accompanying verify.py independently enumerates 24 host cases, 861 roots and checks 780 formal coefficients. Tests do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is a complete membership criterion, a rational bivariate generating function counting DISTINCT concatenated-square roots by their length, and exact even/odd maximizer multiplicities for every q>=2 and k>=1. Inspected primary papers solve general longest-square or periodic-subsequence algorithmic problems (not this complete solution-counting invariant); the shuffle-square paper has a distinct interleaving predicate. Accessible own work counts minimal absent subsequences, scattered palindromes, or expected Abelian square subsequences, none implies this formula. Seven actual published-finding corpus similarity queries yielded no closer direct statement, but unlocated exact specializations remain possible.

value.rationale: Distinct square subsequences have many embeddings but their root count is subtle. A natural infinite family (powers of a full ordered permutation) receives exact membership, a complete length-by-host-period rational enumerator for every alphabet size, and precise parity-sensitive multiplicities of longest solutions. This fully classifies a natural repeated-period benchmark for algorithms; it is not just a routine numeric computation or a one-parameter increment.
